rename.resolution: Not a rename. Theirs-only, and theirs is the outlier — ours already agrees with rclcpp_action and with `action_msgs/msg/GoalStatus`. Re-verdicted to `declined`. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-05 (phase-425): `declined` was the nearest of the five verdicts that existed, and it was still false of the capability. The row is now `their-rename`, the verdict written for exactly this sentence; see `why`.

majority: `action_msgs/msg/GoalStatus` -- the wire type both sides serialize
their_rename.outlier: `rcl_action_goal_state_t` -- rcl alone calls the enum a STATE, while the message it mirrors and the status types beside it in the same header say STATUS

why:
RE-VERDICTED declined -> their-rename 2026-09-05 (phase-425). The W5 re-verdict got the ARGUMENT right and had no verdict to put it under. `declined` reads "ROS 2 has it, we deliberately do not", and we DO have it -- `rclc_goal_status_t`, in all three languages. What we decline is rcl's WORD, which is a different sentence and is what `their-rename` is for. The evidence the W5 text assembled is unchanged and is now in `their_rename`. Pair: `c:goal_status_t`. No code change; no target name invented.

ORIGINAL ROW: RE-VERDICTED rename -> declined 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5). The row's own evidence settles it: rcl is the odd speller. `action_msgs/msg/GoalStatus` is the wire type, and rclcpp_action, our C (`rclc_goal_status_t`), our C++ (`nros::GoalStatus`) and our Rust (`GoalStatus`) all say STATUS; `rcl_action_goal_state_t` says STATE alone. `rename` means OURS is the one that should change, which is false here, so the verdict was wrong even though the prose was right. Declined: rcl has this spelling, we deliberately do not, and the reason is that ours follows the message. No code change; no target name invented. ORIGINAL ROW (verdict was `rename`): rcl's name for what we call `rclc_goal_status_t`, and both mirror `action_msgs/msg/GoalStatus`. rclcpp_action and our C++ and Rust all say STATUS (`GoalStatus`), rcl alone says STATE; ours agrees with the majority and with the message. Recorded as a rename so the pair is visible, but this is one where THEIRS is the odd spelling -- see `c:goal_status_t` for our half.
